title: Sermo I opening: today's joy, David's oracle, and Gabriel's hail
pass_a_gloss: And the mystery which from eternity was hidden, he makes open to us. Today crowns of perennial virtue are woven. Today God, wishing to crown the heads of the benevolent and religious and of those carefully keeping feast days, calls lovers of firm faith as called and heirs; and he calls the upper kingdom with zeal those who taste heavenly things, so that they may join themselves to the divine ministry of the incorporeal choirs. Today the Davidic oracle is fulfilled, which says: Let heavens rejoice and earth exult. Fields will rejoice, and all woods-trees from the Lord's sight, because he comes. And David indeed says woods; but the Forerunner of the Lord names trees making fruits worthy of penitence, rather of the Lord's advent. And our Lord Jesus Christ announces perennial joy to all believing into him. For he says: I will see you and you will rejoice; and your joy no one will take from you. Today the celebrated and ineffable joy of Christians who placed their hope into Christ is announced. Today Gabriel, who assists God, coming to the most chaste Virgin, announces to her that Ave full-of-grace. She indeed thinking with herself what that greeting was, the Angel immediately added saying: The Lord with you. Fear not, Mary; for you found grace with God. Therefore you will conceive in the womb and bear a son; and they will call his name Jesus. This one will be great, and Son of the Most High will be called. And the Lord will give him the seat of David his father, and he will reign in the house of Jacob forever; and of his kingdom there will not be an end. But Mary said to the Angel: How will this be done to me, since I do not know a man? Which things, while as if wondering the most holy Virgin turned with her mind, briefly the Angel brings forth the end of the speech and says: Holy Spirit will come-upon into you, and power of the Most High will overshadow you. And therefore also what will be born from you holy will be called Son of God. For what is, this also altogether will be called. Fittingly therefore holy Mary from all generations alone.
pass_b_english: He makes plain to us the mystery that was hidden from eternity. Today crowns of lasting virtue are woven. Today God, wanting to crown the heads of the kind and devout and of those who carefully keep feast days, names the lovers of firm faith as called ones and heirs; and with eagerness He calls those who set their mind on heavenly things into the upper kingdom, so that they may join themselves to the divine ministry of the bodiless choirs.

Today David's oracle is fulfilled, which says: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult. The fields will be glad, and all the trees of the wood, at the sight of the Lord, for He comes (Psalm 96:11-13). David indeed says trees; but the Forerunner of the Lord names trees that bear fruit worthy of repentance — rather, worthy of the Lord's coming. And our Lord Jesus Christ announces lasting joy to all who believe in Him. For He says: I will see you, and you will rejoice; and your joy no one will take from you (John 16:22).

Today the famous and unspeakable joy of Christians, who have set their hope on Christ, is announced. Today Gabriel, who stands before God, coming to the most chaste Virgin, announces to her that word: Hail, full of grace (Luke 1:28). And while she was thinking within herself what sort of greeting that might be, the Angel at once added, saying: The Lord is with you. Do not fear, Mary; for you have found favor with God. Therefore you will conceive in the womb and bear a son; and they will call His name Jesus. He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord will give Him the throne of David His father, and He will reign in the house of Jacob forever; and of His kingdom there will be no end (Luke 1:30-33).

But Mary said to the Angel: How will this be done to me, since I do not know a man? (Luke 1:34). While the most holy Virgin was turning this over in her mind as if in wonder, the Angel briefly brings the speech to its close and says: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. And therefore the holy one who will be born of you will also be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). For what He is, that He will entirely be called. Fittingly, then, he marks out holy Mary alone from among all generations.
source_text: Mysteriumque quod ab aeterno occultatum fuit, palam nobis facit. Hodie perennis virtutis texuntur coronae. Hodie facta benevolorum et religiosorum, diesque festos studiose colentium capita coronare volens Deus, firmae fidei amatores tanquam vocatos et heredes appellat; supernumque regnum cum studio eos qui caelestia sapiunt, ut se divino incorporeorum chororum ministerio coniungant, vocat. Hodie Davidicum adimpletum est oraculum, quod dicit: Laetentur caeli, et exultet terra. Gaudebunt campi, et omnia ligna silvae a conspectu Domini, quoniam venit. Et David quidem ligna dicit; Praecursor vero Domini arbores facientes fructus dignos paenitentia, immo Domini adventu, nuncupat. Ac Dominus noster Iesus Christus perenne gaudium cunctis in ipsum credentibus adnuntiat. Ait enim: Videbo vos, et gaudebitis; et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis. Hodie celebre atque ineffabile Christianorum gaudium, qui suam in Christum spem posuerunt, adnuntiatur. Hodie Gabriel, qui Deo assistit, ad castissimam Virginem veniens, illud Ave gratia plena ipsi adnuntiat. Ipsa vero secum cogitante qualis esset illa salutatio, Angelus confestim subiunxit, dicens: Dominus tecum. Ne timeas, Maria; invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum. Ideo concipies in utero et paries filium; et vocabunt nomen eius Iesum. Hic erit magnus, et Filius Altissimi vocabitur. Et dabit ipsi Dominus sedem David patris eius, et regnabit in domo Iacob in aeternum; et regni eius non erit finis. Dixit autem Maria ad Angelum: Quomodo istud fiet mihi, quoniam virum non cognosco? Quae, dum velut admirabunda secum animo sanctissima Virgo versaret, breviter Angelus sermonis finem profert, ac dicit: Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi. Ideoque et quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei. Nam quod est, hoc et omnino vocabitur. Convenienter igitur sanctam Mariam ex omnibus generationibus solam.
